title: Admission pruning + burst-inheritance merge conflict causing queued requests to drop KV cache hydration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-severity production outage where a subset of requests from Hosted and Dedicated customers were admitted but never processed, leading to sustained 502/503s, large KV cache miss amplification, and elevated costs. Root cause traced to a merge conflict between ingress policy inheritance and the admission-pruning scheduler that caused queued requests to be dropped before they populated the KV cache.
timeline:

2026-02-05 09:45 UTC: Scoped to admission-service + orchestrator interaction; enabled request tracing.
2026-02-05 10:30 UTC: Hotfix: temporary bypass to force explicit tenant policy precedence deployed to Hosted to stop further drops.
2026-02-06 02:10 UTC: Full fix deployed to admission controller and reconciler; rolling restart of orchestrator nodes to flush stale queue state.
2026-02-08 14:00 UTC: Follow-up E2E tests and monitoring added.

impact: Affected 4 enterprise customers in Hosted and 2 Dedicated tenants for 6-8 hours of degraded service (2026-02-05 09:12 - 2026-02-05 17:30 UTC). Peak error rate: +12,400 5xx/min across affected regions. Requests that were dropped experienced double compute/cost due to repeated client retries and extra cold KV-cache misses. SLA breach investigation opened for two customers.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create tenant with inherited burst profile from dedicated overlay and enabled admission-pruning TTL shorter than orchestrator queue stall time.
2) Generate sustained burst of requests that exceed short-term token bucket but are permitted by inherited burst window.
3) Simulate orchestrator node restart during the burst and observe admission service pruning logic removing entries whose admission_epoch field is compared against token_bucket_epoch instead of admission_epoch.
4) Observe accepted requests drop without processing; KV cache misses increase on subsequent retries.
root_cause: Two independent changes combined to produce the outage: (a) a behavior change in config-merger where 'inherited_burst_profile' from Dedicated overlays was incorrectly promoted over explicit tenant policy if the overlay had non-null 'priority_hint' (regression introduced in runtime-1.20), and (b) an admission-pruning bug where the scheduler used token_bucket_epoch for pruning decisions instead of admission_epoch during orchestrator handoff. The result: requests were marked admitted by the admission controller but later pruned by the scheduler because epochs didn't match, leaving the orchestrator queue in a state where entries were dropped before processing and before KV cache hydration could occur.
mitigation:
- Immediate: Deployed a hotfix that enforces explicit tenant policy precedence and increased admission queue TTL from 3s to 12s for affected regions.
- Short term: Applied per-tenant burst bypass for the 6 impacted customers to restore throughput while fix rolled out.
- Operational: Scaled up orchestrator workers (2x) to reduce restart windows and drained affected nodes with a controlled drain procedure.
permanent_fix:
1) Fix config-merger to never allow overlay 'priority_hint' to override explicit tenant burst policy. Unit + integration tests added.
2) Correct admission-pruner epoch comparison to use admission_epoch consistently; added deterministic contract tests to prevent epoch drift regressions.
3) Add e2e test that exercises orchestrator restart during bursts to validate end-to-end KV cache hydration and admission behavior.
4) Deployment: release runtime-1.21 with the fixes; require canary on Hosted then Dedicated then Private.
rollback_plan: If the runtime-1.21 rollout shows regressions: revert the admission-pruner change first (safe-mode) and keep explicit tenant precedence hotfix in place, then revert config-merger fix only if necessary. We maintain playbooks for manual per-tenant bypass toggles and an automated circuit-breaker to move traffic to secondary region.
monitoring_and_alerting: Added metrics: admission.pruned_count, admission.epoch_mismatch_rate, orchestrator.queue_drop_rate, kvcache.miss_ratio_post_admit. Alert thresholds: admission.epoch_mismatch_rate > 1% for 5m triggers page. Dashboards: admission vs orchestrator correlation graph and per-tenant burst inheritance map.
